business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Aseptic Tubing of Ambient Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law provinces; Civil Law in Quebec; federal statutory corporate and food-safety regimes)

Canada–EU Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (SC 2000, c 17), as amended; Canada Business Corporations Act (RSC 1985, c C-44), s 21.1–21.4 (Individuals with Significant Control register); FINTRAC Guidance, including Politically Exposed Persons policy; Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17); United Nations Act (RSC 1985, c U-2); Corporations Canada compliance and enforcement practice.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against the United Nations Consolidated List, Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act (administered by Global Affairs Canada and enforced by FINTRAC and OSFI), and supplementary OFAC SDN List screening on account of USD Swift_LC and TT_Wire correspondent banking; mandatory PEP determination, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and heads of international organizations, with enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring per PCMLTFA and FINTRAC policy; risk-tier classification for this commercial profile is Low_Risk_Standard subject to standard verification and source-of-funds documentation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (E-filing with integrated NUANS Name Search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English, French, or bilingual; every name must be distinctive, not deceptively misdescriptive, and include a mandatory legal element (Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, Inc., Corp., Ltée, Ltd.); Arabic or Roman numerals are permitted; names in a language other than English or French must be accompanied by an English or French transliteration; a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report is required for all proposed federal corporate names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Olympic (protected under the Olympic and Paralympic Marks Act)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Federal name reservations are valid for 90 days and cannot be extended; if incorporation lapses, a new NUANS report and reservation must be filed. Upon refusal of a name, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director appointed under the Canada Business Corporations Act, attaching a revised NUANS report and distinguishing evidence; if the Director maintains the refusal, file an application with the Federal Court within 21 days of notice of refusal seeking an order directing incorporation under the proposed name, pursuant to s 9 of the CBCA.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office accepted for the CBCA registered office if a physical street address is maintained by the registered agent for service of process and records, and the address is in the province named in the articles; however, for a licensed food-manufacturing establishment producing canned boba tapioca pearls, a virtual office cannot satisfy CFIA commercial-substance requirements, and a physically occupied, municipally zoned processing facility with a Preventive Control Plan is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (approximately 85–90% within the first operating year); CFIA conducts routine and unannounced inspections of licensed establishments handling thermally processed and aseptically tubed low-acid foods, with additional municipal and provincial food-safety inspection exposure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including sections 5–7 (incorporation), 19–20 (corporate records and registered office), 24–25 (shares and consideration), 106 (directors), and 173 (articles amendments).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, a directorate of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, Form 1 under the CBCA, submitted through Corporations Canada's Online Filing Centre.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital or paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration approved by the directors, subject to CBCA section 25; consideration must be received before issuance. No incorporation-related escrow account is prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscriptions for the shares set out in the subscription agreements, issue those shares upon receipt of the agreed consideration, and enter the issuances in its securities register. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office be established at [full address in the province or territory stated in the articles]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [name] be appointed Secretary, and [name] be authorized to execute and submit required corporate, tax, banking, and licensing documents. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the officers are authorized to take all actions necessary to implement these resolutions, subject to the CBCA, the articles, and the bylaws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select federal incorporation terms and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED; Online Filing Centre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a numbered or word corporate name and identify the province or territory for the registered office. A federal corporation must maintain its registered office in the province or territory specified in its articles. For a word name, obtain a NUANS name search report and use a name that meets CBCA and Corporations Canada requirements. No notarization is ordinarily required for online incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-name selection
NUANS report for a proposed word name, where required
Registered office address
Director names and addresses for service
Share structure and any transfer restrictions or other provisions
Incorporator identification and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected, submit an acceptable revised name or use a numbered name. Correct incomplete or inconsistent articles and resubmit through the portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File articles and obtain the certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED; Online Filing Centre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 1 electronically, pay the applicable fee, and retain the certificate and filed articles. The ordinary online federal incorporation fee is CAD 200; the USD figure shown is an approximate conversion, not a fixed USD fee. Filing is generally electronic and does not require notarization. Processing times are subject to Corporations Canada's current service standard.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation, Form 1
NUANS report, if applicable
Payment details for the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any Corporations Canada request through the filing channel, correct the identified information, and pay any applicable resubmission or additional service fee. Confirm that the corrected certificate and articles have been issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organize the corporation and establish statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's first directors and registered office; Corporations Canada for applicable statutory filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting or obtain written resolutions. Adopt bylaws, appoint officers, approve share subscriptions and issuances, establish the registered office, approve banking authority, and create the required corporate registers and records. Issue shares only upon receipt of the agreed consideration. File the initial registered-office and first-director information within the CBCA-prescribed period, generally 60 days after incorporation, using Corporations Canada's online services. Maintain the individuals with significant control register and file required information with Corporations Canada, subject to statutory exceptions.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and filed articles
First board resolutions and bylaws
Share subscription agreements and evidence of consideration
Securities register and individuals with significant control information
Registered office and director information
Officer and banking authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registers and resolutions promptly, file overdue required information, and assess applicable penalties or compliance exposure. Obtain corporate legal advice where an omitted filing or defective share issuance requires ratification or corrective filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register extra-provincially and complete tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate registry of each province or territory where the corporation carries on business; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine extra-provincial registration, name, annual-return, and local registered-office requirements in each operating jurisdiction and complete registrations before commencing activities where required. Obtain a CRA business number and register for a corporate income tax program account; assess GST/HST, payroll, and import-export accounts as applicable. Provincial or territorial registrations and taxes are separate from federal incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate and articles of incorporation
Registered office and Canadian service-address details required by the jurisdiction
Director and officer information
Business activities and anticipated commencement date
CRA business registration information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Complete missing registrations or tax accounts and respond to registry or CRA requests for supporting information. Confirm jurisdiction-specific late fees, filing deadlines, and any restrictions on carrying on business before registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) for applicable federal food licensing and food-safety requirements; provincial or territorial food-safety authorities and municipal permitting authorities for local premises and operations. Canada has no general federal industrial licensing board for this manufacturing activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians licence (SFCR licence), where required under the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations for interprovincial trade, export, or other regulated activities. A licence is not automatically required solely because food is manufactured and sold within one province; confirm the activity and product-specific requirements with CFIA.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (IAAC); Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) administers relevant federal environmental statutes and regulations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No automatic federal impact assessment is established for this activity. A federal impact assessment is required only if the project is designated under the Impact Assessment Act or otherwise brought within its application. Provincial or territorial environmental assessment screening may apply based on location, scale, and project characteristics.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: There is no single Canada-wide numeric wastewater or VOC threshold applicable to every facility. Obtain applicable provincial or territorial environmental approvals and municipal sewer-use authorization before discharge; comply with site-specific effluent limits, pretreatment requirements, and applicable federal rules. Classify, store, transport, and dispose of solid and hazardous waste under applicable provincial or territorial requirements and federal cross-border movement rules. Assess air-emission permits and controls under the laws of the facility's province or territory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupancy and production, obtain applicable municipal building, zoning, occupancy, and fire approvals; complete required fire-protection and life-safety inspections; and verify floor and equipment structural loads through qualified professionals where required by building approvals. Comply with the province or territory's occupational health and safety legislation, worker training, machine guarding, chemical-handling, and workplace inspection requirements. Requirements and issuing authorities vary by site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) and CRA My Business Account (MyBA); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) is the joint customs/export administrator.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident corporation forming or operating a Canadian business: (1) confirm whether it is required or eligible to register for GST/HST, including whether the small supplier threshold of CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies has been exceeded in the preceding four calendar quarters; (2) apply through CRA Business Registration Online or paper Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number and Certain Accounts'; (3) CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST program account (RT) if registration is approved; (4) for non-resident registrants, CRA may require security or bond before the GST/HST account becomes active; (5) use the BN on all CRA filings, customs export declarations, import/export records, sales invoices and tax remittances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Canadian federal corporate tax law; an incorporated entity is always taxed as a corporation under Part I of the Income Tax Act. Relevant elections include the functional currency election under ITA s. 261, capital cost allowance elections, and certain GST/HST elections for branch accounting and reporting periods.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (federal GST is 5%; participating provinces add a harmonized provincial component).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide GST/HST taxable supplies in the immediately preceding four calendar quarters (small supplier threshold); registration becomes mandatory once this threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal real-time clearance, tax approval, or digital stamping mandate exists for e-invoicing in Canada. CRA permits paper and readable electronic invoices, including EDI, XML and PDF, provided they contain: seller legal name and GST/HST business number, recipient name, date, description, quantity, consideration, applicable tax rate, and tax payable or explicit zero-rating/exemption indication. Electronic records must be preserved and made accessible to CRA on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Canned boba tapioca pearls exported from Canada qualify for zero-rating under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when the supply is made to a non-resident and the goods are shipped or delivered outside Canada, whether by the exporter or through a carrier/customs broker, with export occurring in normal commercial course. The exporter must retain documentary evidence of Canadian export and non-Canadian destination. Services supplied to non-residents that are not related to Canadian real property or tangible personal property are generally deemed supplied outside Canada and therefore not subject to GST/HST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) declaration or CBSA export confirmation
Commercial invoice prepared on supplier letterhead
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill showing Canadian origin and foreign destination
Packing list evidencing the exported goods
Sales contract or purchase order from the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent SWIFT/TT payment receipt evidencing foreign-currency settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess and claw back claimed export zero-rating where the documentary bundle is deficient, goods are not exported within a reasonable period, or the supply is determined to have been made in Canada. Penalties include reassessed GST/HST net tax, compounded daily prescribed interest, a civil penalty of CAD 500 plus 50% of any net tax understatement for false or misleading statements made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence, and criminal liability for tax evasion under s. 327 of the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency regime under the Bank of Canada Act. Both current and capital accounts are freely convertible with no prior approval required for profit remittances. Hurdles are limited to FINTRAC AML reporting thresholds and beneficial ownership verification; no capital controls apply to standard corporate remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts must be repatriated to Canada within 90 days. No mandatory surrender or fixed conversion ratio exists; funds convert at prevailing market rates. Statutory reporting via Export Reporting System and bank channels is mandatory for all receipts exceeding CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is low due to FINTRAC and OSFI regulatory oversight. Offshore digital EMIs permitted only via licensed Canadian bank partnerships or Payment Services Act-compliant fintechs; legal constraints include mandatory KYC/AML and potential licensing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signers must attend physical KYC interviews for initial corporate account opening. Remote opening is permitted for select low-risk accounts but prohibited for cross-border treasury, FX, or high-value setups.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or assets
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements, audited financials, export contracts, and director affidavits detailing business activity
Corporate ownership chart, shareholder agreements, and updated beneficial ownership registry filings

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to high-risk jurisdictions or sectors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply chain due diligence, import/export licenses, and third-party verification of tapioca sourcing

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY INFUSION'. Verification requires board resolutions, share purchase agreements, and source-of-funds documentation. All transactions over CAD 10,000 must comply with FINTRAC reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared via SWIFT MT103 (purpose codes 'EXPORT PAYMENT' or 'TRADE SETTLEMENT') and Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. For tapioca pearl exports, ensure compliance with Canadian export controls and destination-country import regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under CBCA s. 263
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late-fee regime; default for two consecutive years may trigger a Director's notice and administrative dissolution after a 120-day cure period; CBCA s. 250 summary conviction fine up to CAD 5,000

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 6th month after the end of the corporation's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeated failure penalties up to 10%; no administrative strike-off from the CRA filing regime

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for CBCA distributing corporations whose securities are part of a distribution to the public; private/non-distributing corporations may dispense with an appointed auditor only by unanimous shareholder resolution. No CBCA revenue or asset threshold requires audit; lender or article requirements may compel an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; private/non-distributing corporations may elect ASPE or IFRS as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under CBCA Part 21.1, non-distributing corporations must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC). No separate annual UBO filing is made to Corporations Canada; the annual return includes an officer attestation that the register is accurate and current. Any share transfer or significant-control event must be recorded in the register within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware of the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
Minute Book of shareholder and directors' resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (federal general corporate rate; rates vary by province from 8% to 16%, producing a combined general rate of approximately 23% to 31%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction: 9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC); full expensing (100% CCA) for new manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment acquired before 2028; SR&ED refundable investment tax credit of 35% for CCPCs (15% non-refundable for large corporations); exempt surplus/ foreign affiliate dividend deductions.
